title: RES Branch 5 — Integration: Harvested Data → Manufacturing Domain Engines
description: 8 milestones that connect harvested resource data to specific manufacturing domains. These milestones consume outputs from earlier RES harvesting milestones (MS0-MS15) and wire them into domain-specific intelligence engines: probing, fixturing, setup sheets, customer defaults, materials, drawings, NC output, and hyperMILL automation. Each milestone produces a Forge-Triple (protective hook + MCP action + skill).

milestones.title: Probing Routine Selection Engine — 5,753 Cycles + Machine Configs

tribal: Renishaw EP+IP probing on 3 JM Die mills
Blum Quickstart 469 cycles on Roku-Roku
Okuma OSP probing conventions
JM Die probing folder patterns in POSTS AND MACHINES/

milestones.intent: The machinist selects a part feature (bore, boss, plane, pocket, web) and machine, and PRISM automatically selects the correct probing routine from 5,753 available cycles. It knows Renishaw EP+IP runs on the Hurco, Haas, and one Okuma mill, while Blum Quickstart (469 cycles!) drives the Roku-Roku. No more hunting through cycle files — PRISM picks the right probe routine for the right machine.

U-PRB01.title: Build ProbingCycleIndexEngine — classify 5,753 .cyc probing cycles by feature type + probe system
U-PRB01.description: Index all 5,753 .cyc files from POSTS AND MACHINES/ that relate to probing. Classify each cycle by: (1) probe system (Renishaw EP, Renishaw IP, Blum Quickstart, OMP, generic), (2) feature type (bore, boss, web, pocket, plane, corner, angle, single-point), (3) measurement mode (WCS setting, in-process verification, tool length, tool breakage), (4) axis requirements (3-axis, 4-axis, 5-axis), (5) machine association from folder path. Build searchable index keyed by [machine + feature_type + measurement_mode].

Feature type classification >95% accuracy
Probe system identified for each cycle
Machine association resolved from folder path

abort_criteria: Probe system unresolvable for >10% of cycles

U-PRB03.title: Build ProbingRoutineSelectionEngine — select optimal probe routine from feature + machine + tolerance

smart_config.role: CNC Post Processor Engineer + Output Format Specialist

tribal: OPEN MIND NcGenerator handles G-code translation per controller
9 CNC controller configs with dialect-specific rules
Report Generator produces formatted output docs per language/template
JM Die runs Okuma OSP, Haas NGC, Hurco WinMAX, Fanuc 31i-B5, Mitsubishi
reference: OPEN MIND/NcGenerator/ (9 controller configs with G-code translation tables)
OPEN MIND/Report Generator/ (15 languages x 9 XSLT templates)

milestones.intent: PRISM understands the exact output format for every CNC controller in the shop. When generating NC code for the Okuma LB3000, it produces OSP-compatible output with correct G85/G87 boring cycles, M-code coolant control, and Okuma-specific tool offset format. For the Haas VF-2SS, it outputs NGC-compatible code with Haas-specific probing cycles and setting references. The Report Generator templates provide formatted job documentation in the operator's preferred language.

U-NCF01.title: Build NcGeneratorParserEngine — parse 9 controller configs into G-code translation rules
U-NCF01.description: Parse OPEN MIND NcGenerator configs for each of the 9 CNC controller families: (1) Extract G-code translation tables (generic G-code → controller-specific G-code), (2) Extract M-code mappings per controller (coolant, spindle, clamp, ATC), (3) Extract format rules (line numbering, block structure, comment syntax, decimal precision), (4) Extract safety block templates (program start, program end, tool change, emergency stop), (5) Map each config to controllers in JM Die's shop (Okuma OSP config → 7 Okuma lathes + 1 mill). Build NcTranslationRuleSet per controller family.
